This study compares two insulin regimens (lispro mixtures vs glargine) in patients already receiving metformin. Both treatment arms include metformin, so there is no comparison of metformin vs non-metformin therapy. Additionally, the outcomes focus on HbA1c and hypoglycemia, not lactic acidosis risk.

This randomized trial compares NPL insulin vs glargine insulin added to stable metformin/sulfonylurea regimens. Both treatment arms receive metformin, so metformin is not being evaluated against a non-metformin comparator. Outcomes are glycemic control and hypoglycemia, not lactic acidosis.

This study compares extended-release metformin vs immediate-release metformin. Both arms receive metformin (different formulations), so there is no comparison of metformin vs non-metformin therapy. The study does not assess lactic acidosis risk.

This placebo-controlled study evaluates adding glipizide GITS to metformin vs adding placebo to metformin. Both treatment arms continue metformin, so metformin itself is not being compared to non-metformin therapy. The study does not report lactic acidosis outcomes.

This post-hoc analysis compares basal+prandial insulin mixtures vs basal insulin glargine in patients already treated with metformin. All patients receive metformin, so there is no metformin vs non-metformin comparison. Outcomes focus on glycemic variability, not lactic acidosis.
